newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends steady, Brent climbs with NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends steady, Brent climbs with NYMEX.

text.p: IPE gas oil ended the session barely changed on Wednesday despite fairly strong gains on Brent futures.
April gas oil closed 25 cents up at $172.50 a tonne, while May Brent was trading 32 cents up at the end of gas oil's session.
"Gas oil has been relatively strong in relation to Brent over the last couple of days, so Brent was catching up with that," one dealer said.
Brent's steady rally was attributed to a strong performance by NYMEX crude and products futures.
The May Brent/gas oil crack spread stood at $3.47 a barrel.
"Gasoline is the contract that everyone is looking at and that made some good gains," a broker said.
NYMEX April unleaded gasoline raded 0.83 cents up at 67.35 a gallon at 1738 GMT, after the Energy Information Agency (EIA) weekly data showed a draw on gasoline stocks of 900,000 barrels.
The EIA figures also showed that stocks were still eight million barrels below year-ago levels with the peak driving season fast approaching.
Brokers said that a key reversal on NYMEX crude on Wednesday was a positive sign.
May NYMEX crude managed to climb back above $21, having slipped below the key psychological level earlier in the day.

EIA data showing a crude draw of 1.1 million barrels, compared to a draw of 2.2 million barrels shown by earlier figures from the American Petroleum Institute (API) momentarily dented confidence, dealers said.
"WTI made a good recovery and technically it looks like we could have turned a corner," said one broker.
On Brent, dealers saw next resistance at $19.86 and then at $20 a barrel. "If we manage to get above $19.86 today it could be quite constructive," said one.
